# Fairpractice Staff Licenses (`fairpractice-staff-licenses`)

Checks staff licenses and certifications (nursing and allied licenses, BLS, ACLS and others): expired or expiring, required for the role but missing, never or not recently verified at the source, licenses that do not cover the state worked, and shifts worked on an expired credential. Staff names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Staff Licenses never changes the schedule or anyone's status; a manager does. Fairpractice Staff Licenses never reports anyone to a licensing board.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-staff-licenses demo
npx -y fairpractice-staff-licenses mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Regional (a made-up hospital) and made-up staff. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`credentials.csv`](fixtures/credentials.csv): one row per license or certificate. Planted: an RN license that expired on 2026-10-31 with three shifts worked after it (N202), a BLS card that expired in September (N203), an RN license expiring in December (N203), a single-state California license for a nurse working in Texas (N204), an LVN license never verified (N205), a BLS card last verified in February 2025 (N201) and a respiratory therapist with no BLS (R301).
- [`roster.csv`](fixtures/roster.csv): active staff with work state; the terminated nurse is skipped.
- [`shifts.csv`](fixtures/shifts.csv): shifts worked in October and November.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): required credentials per role, 60-day warning, yearly re-verification, the compact states the hospital relies on (example only; check the current member list) and which credentials are state licenses. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `licenses_check` | List expired, missing, unverified and wrong-state credentials, and shifts worked on an expired one. | runs |
| `licenses_write_report` | Write licenses.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and licenses.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/licenses). | runs |
| `licenses_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `licenses_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `licenses_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `licenses_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `schedule_remove` | Fairpractice Staff Licenses never changes the schedule or anyone's status; a manager does. | refused |
| `board_report_submit` | Fairpractice Staff Licenses never reports anyone to a licensing board. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `licenses_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `credentials` (required) | Credentials file under --root: one row per license or certificate with person, role, credential, state, expiry, verification date and multistate flag |
| `roster` | Optional active staff roster: person id, name, role, department and work state (finds required credentials that are missing) |
| `shifts` | Optional worked shifts: person id, date and work state (finds shifts worked on an expired credential) |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: required_by_role, warn_days, verify_days, compact_states, state_licensed |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-staff-licenses inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Credentials (`credentials`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |
| `name` | text (masked) | Employee, Employee Name, Staff, Staff Name, Name, Full Name, Worker, Caregiver |
| `role` | text | Role, Job Title, Title, Position, Job, Discipline, Job Code |
| `department` | text | Department, Dept, Unit, Location, Site, Cost Center, Clinic |
| `credential` (required) | text | Credential, License, License Type, Certification, Cert, Credential Type, Document |
| `number` | text | License #, License Number, Number, Cert #, Credential Number |
| `state` | text | State, Issuing State, License State, Issued By |
| `expires` | date | Expires, Expiration, Expiration Date, Exp Date, Expiry, Valid Through |
| `verified_on` | date | Verified, Verified On, Verification Date, Primary Source Verified, PSV Date, Last Verified |
| `compact` | text | Compact, Multistate, Multi-State, License Scope, NLC |

### Staff roster (`roster`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` (required) | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |
| `name` | text (masked) | Employee, Employee Name, Staff, Staff Name, Name, Full Name, Worker, Caregiver |
| `role` | text | Role, Job Title, Title, Position, Job, Discipline, Job Code |
| `department` | text | Department, Dept, Unit, Location, Site, Cost Center, Clinic |
| `work_state` | text | Work State, Practice State, Shift State, Location State, State Worked |
| `status` | text | Status, Employment Status, State, Current Status |

### Worked shifts (`shifts`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` (required) | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |
| `date` (required) | date | Date, Shift Date, Work Date, Punch Date |
| `work_state` | text | Work State, Practice State, Shift State, Location State, State Worked |

## Settings file (`licenses_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `required_by_role` | Credentials each role must hold, e.g. {"RN": ["RN License", "BLS"]} |
| `warn_days` | Days before expiry to start warning; default 60 |
| `verify_days` | Days after which a primary-source verification counts as stale; default 365 |
| `compact_states` | Two-letter states in the license compact you rely on (check the current member list) |
| `state_licensed` | Credential names that are state licenses, so the work state is checked |

## Memory

`licenses_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `licenses_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-staff-licenses": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-staff-licenses",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-staff-licenses -- npx -y fairpractice-staff-licenses mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-staff-licenses tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-staff-licenses sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-staff-licenses inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-staff-licenses call licenses_check '{"credentials":"<credentials>"}'
fairpractice-staff-licenses eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-staff-licenses demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
